title: Qes Beqes (Slowly, Slowly)
logline: A girl learning to bake injera wants to quit after her first torn attempts, until her mother puts an egg in her palm and reminds her how slowly good things grow.
feel: Relief and permission to go slowly: small steady steps count as progress.
style_block: flat illustrated storybook style, warm earth tones of ochre, terracotta and cream, soft paper texture, gentle morning light, no text, no letters

characters.girl: a 12-year-old Ethiopian girl with black braided hair, large expressive brown eyes, a mustard-yellow dress and a white cotton shawl over her shoulders
characters.mother: her mother, an Ethiopian woman in her late thirties with warm brown skin and a kind face, wearing a plain white cotton dress with a green-and-red embroidered border and a plain white headscarf, always the same white outfit

setting: a small traditional Ethiopian home kitchen with mud-plastered walls and a clay floor, a round clay mitad griddle on a low stove, a woven basket of eggs, one small window with warm sunlight; no modern cabinets, no sink, no electric appliances. Injera is a large round spongy pale grey-beige flatbread covered in tiny bubble holes
